title: 214(b): presumed to be leaving forever
category_name: Visas, consulate queues and the money spent on being told no
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: US law presumes every visitor-visa applicant intends to immigrate. The applicant must disprove a presumption about his own mind. For Mexicans this single subsection is the overwhelming majority of refusals, and there is no appeal from it.

title: The appointment that is eighteen months away
category_name: Visas, consulate queues and the money spent on being told no
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Even a successful application is rationed by calendar. Post-pandemic backlogs at Mexican consulates reached multi-year waits, which converts a visa into a thing you plan your life around rather than apply for.

title: The ten-year bar you trigger by applying honestly
category_name: Visas, consulate queues and the money spent on being told no
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Unlawful presence in the US creates a three- or ten-year bar on return. The bar is triggered by departing - so the man who leaves voluntarily to do it properly is the one who gets barred.

title: The border crossing card, and the line it draws
category_name: Visas, consulate queues and the money spent on being told no
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The BCC/laser visa permits short visits within a limited zone. It is the most common US visa held by Mexicans and it is explicitly not permission to work, live, or go far inland.

title: CURP, acta, and proving you were born
category_name: Passport, CURP, acta de nacimiento: proving who you are
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Mexican administrative life runs on the CURP and a certified birth certificate. A man whose birth was registered late, in another state, or with an inconsistent name spends years reconciling himself.

title: A passport that is fine, and a nationality that is the problem
category_name: Passport, CURP, acta de nacimiento: proving who you are
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The Mexican passport is functional and reasonably ranked. The hurdle is not the booklet - it is that the nationality on it changes the question being asked at every counter.

title: The papers you no longer have
category_name: Passport, CURP, acta de nacimiento: proving who you are
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Deportation, detention and robbery strip people of the documents their subsequent life requires, at the exact moment they have least capacity to replace them.

title: The second room
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the second room
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Secondary inspection: referral out of the primary queue into a room with no clock, no phone and no lawyer. The brief asked specifically about unusually high rates of 'random checks' - this issue records what is actually documented and what is not.

title: Your phone, at the border, without a warrant
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the second room
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The border search exception removes the warrant requirement. Messages, photographs, contacts and drafts are readable, and refusing costs more for a visa holder than for a citizen.

title: Being the passenger the airline worries about
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the second room
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Carrier sanctions push the first check upstream: the airline decides at the gate whether it believes a passenger will be admitted, because the airline pays if he is not.

title: The deadliest land crossing in the world
category_name: The border: crossing it, being turned around, dying on it
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The US-Mexico border is the most lethal overland migration route on record, and the lethality is a product of routing people into desert.

title: Turned around at the bridge
category_name: The border: crossing it, being turned around, dying on it
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A visa is permission to apply for entry, not permission to enter. The port-of-entry decision is final, unreviewable, and made in minutes.

title: Coming home, and the desk at that end too
category_name: The border: crossing it, being turned around, dying on it
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Mexican customs and the return leg have their own discretion - the aduana button, the vehicle inspection, and the question of what he is bringing back.

title: Put down in a dangerous city, after dark
category_name: Deportation, removal and being put down somewhere at night
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Deportation is not only removal; it is a delivery, to a specific place, at a specific hour. Newly deported men are a preferred target for kidnapping and extortion, and the timing of release is what makes them findable.

title: Lateral repatriation: sent back somewhere you have never been
category_name: Deportation, removal and being put down somewhere at night
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Being returned not to where you crossed or where you are from, but to whichever port is operationally convenient - which can be two thousand kilometres from anyone who knows you.

title: The family that stays behind the line
category_name: Deportation, removal and being put down somewhere at night
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Removal separates a household across a border one half cannot cross and the other half cannot re-enter, indefinitely.

title: Served, then deported
category_name: Deported veterans: served, then removed
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Lawful permanent residents who served in the US military, were told service meant citizenship, and were removed anyway - frequently for offences connected to untreated service injuries.

title: The undocumented years
category_name: Status in the US: the undocumented years, DACA, the waiting
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Living and working for a decade or more with no status: paying tax, raising citizens, and being removable at any moment for the whole period.

title: Status that can be cancelled by announcement
category_name: Status in the US: the undocumented years, DACA, the waiting
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: DACA, TPS and parole are revocable programmes rather than status. People build lives on them and the ground can be withdrawn by policy change rather than by anything they did.

title: Detained, with no right to a lawyer
category_name: Status in the US: the undocumented years, DACA, the waiting
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Immigration detention is civil, not criminal - which means no public defender, no right to appointed counsel, and detention in a facility that may be a thousand miles from any family.

title: The visa that belongs to the employer
category_name: Work abroad: wage theft, the sponsor, the day-labour corner
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: H-2A and H-2B visas are tied to a single employer. Leaving a bad job means leaving the country, which is the entire leverage.

title: The corner, and being paid at the end of the day or not
category_name: Work abroad: wage theft, the sponsor, the day-labour corner
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Day labour: hired from a street corner by a stranger in a truck, with no contract, no record, and no way to enforce payment.

title: Named on the CV, before anyone reads it
category_name: Work abroad: wage theft, the sponsor, the day-labour corner
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Name-based screening in hiring, and the accent on the phone.

title: The highest workplace death rate of any group
category_name: The body at work: injury, heat, height, and what it costs
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Hispanic and Latino workers in the US have had the highest fatal injury rate of any group for eight consecutive years, and most of those deaths are foreign-born men.

title: Back pain as an occupational outcome
category_name: The body at work: injury, heat, height, and what it costs
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: The brief asked about back pain specifically. It is measured in Latino manual workers, and the association with job precariousness - not just lifting - is the finding that matters.

title: Heat
category_name: The body at work: injury, heat, height, and what it costs
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Outdoor work in rising temperatures, with water, shade and rest breaks contested rather than guaranteed.

title: Sixty billion dollars, and what it costs to send it
category_name: Remittances: the money sent, and what sending it costs
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Remittances are the visible product of the whole arrangement. The flow is enormous, the fees are a levy on the poorest transfers, and in 2025 it fell for the first time in over a decade.

title: The one who left, and what he is now for
category_name: Remittances: the money sent, and what sending it costs
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Being the household's income from a distance reorganises a man's place in his own family into a function.

title: More than half the workforce is informal
category_name: The informal economy, the wage, and the length of the day
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Informality is not a fringe - it is the majority condition of Mexican work, and it means no contract, no social security and no pension.

title: Second in the OECD for hours worked
category_name: The informal economy, the wage, and the length of the day
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: The Mexican working year is among the longest in the developed world, which is the hidden term in every comparison of Mexican wages to anyone else's.

title: Nine in ten of the dead are men
category_name: Homicide and armed violence, and who it actually kills
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Mexican homicide is overwhelmingly the killing of young men. The figure is stable across three decades and is the single most important number in this dataset.

title: Being the demographic
category_name: Homicide and armed violence, and who it actually kills
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: A young man in certain states is read by police, employers, landlords and border officers as a member of a category before he is read as a person - by the same statistics that describe him as the likeliest victim.

title: The reporter who is killed for the story
category_name: Homicide and armed violence, and who it actually kills
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Mexico is repeatedly ranked among the deadliest countries on earth for journalists, and the killing is mostly unsolved.

title: Over a hundred thousand people, not found
category_name: Disappearance, the searching, and the graves
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Mexico's registry of disappeared and missing persons is among the largest in the world outside active warfare, and roughly three quarters of it is men.

title: The mothers who dig
category_name: Disappearance, the searching, and the graves
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Because the state does not search effectively, families - mostly mothers and sisters of missing men - search themselves, with rods and shovels, and find the graves.

title: Ayotzinapa: forty-three, and a state that lied about it
category_name: Disappearance, the searching, and the graves
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: The disappearance of 43 male students in 2014, the fabricated official account, and a decade of confirmed obstruction - the case that demonstrates what happens when a disappearance is too big to bury.

title: The job advertisement that is a trap
category_name: Cartels: recruitment, forced labour and the fake job ad
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Forced recruitment of young men through fake job postings offering security work at above-market pay - the mechanism uncovered at Teuchitlán in 2025.

title: Taxed by whoever holds the road
category_name: Cartels: recruitment, forced labour and the fake job ad
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Territorial control exercised as a levy on movement and trade - the closest thing in this dataset to the brief's word 'occupied'.

title: La Bestia, and being cargo
category_name: Transit through Mexico: the train, the kidnap, the ransom
applies_to_note: Triggered by being male
summary: Transit migrants riding freight trains through Mexico - mostly young men - exposed to mutilation, kidnapping and extortion along the whole length of the country.

title: San Fernando: two hundred and sixty-five people
category_name: Transit through Mexico: the train, the kidnap, the ransom
applies_to_note: Triggered by being male
summary: The 2010 and 2011 massacres in Tamaulipas, the police involvement, and the fact that they remain effectively unpunished.

title: The migrants who are not Mexican, in Mexico
category_name: Transit through Mexico: the train, the kidnap, the ransom
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Mexico as a transit and now destination country, including flows the brief asked about from outside the Americas.

title: Beaten into saying it
category_name: Police, military, torture and arbitrary detention
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Torture and ill-treatment in Mexican custody is not anecdotal - it has been measured by the national statistics institute, in a survey of the prison population, and the numbers are extraordinary.

title: The soldier doing police work
category_name: Police, military, torture and arbitrary detention
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Two decades of military deployment for domestic public security, with troops trained for war carrying out stops, searches and arrests.

title: Reporting a crime, and what it costs to bother
category_name: Police, military, torture and arbitrary detention
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: The cifra negra: the overwhelming majority of crime in Mexico is never reported, and the reason is a rational assessment of what reporting achieves.

title: Arraigo and being held before being charged
category_name: Police, military, torture and arbitrary detention
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Pre-charge detention for investigation, long criticised internationally, which inverts the normal sequence of accusation and evidence.

title: Imprisoned without a sentence
category_name: The justice system: pretrial detention, arraigo, the prison
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Automatic pretrial detention - prisión preventiva oficiosa - jails people on the category of the accusation rather than on any individual assessment. Roughly half of Mexico's unsentenced prisoners are held this way.

title: The overcrowded cell
category_name: The justice system: pretrial detention, arraigo, the prison
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Mexican prisons at record population with overcrowding concentrated in a subset of facilities, holding a population that is over 90% male.

title: A record that closes the rest of his life
category_name: The justice system: pretrial detention, arraigo, the prison
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Carta de no antecedentes penales: the certificate of no criminal record, demanded for formal work, which converts one prosecution into permanent exclusion.

title: The ball draw
category_name: Conscription: the ball draw, and the year the state takes
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Mexico conscripts by lottery, and only men are obliged to enter it. A year of Saturdays is allocated by drawing a coloured ball from a drum - one of the few hurdles in any of these datasets that applies to men and only men, explicitly, by law.

title: Cobro de piso: paying to be allowed to trade
category_name: Extortion, cobro de piso and the trades that get taxed
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: A weekly levy on small businesses, enforced by threat, which falls on the trades men predominantly run - shops, transport, farms, workshops.

title: The trades that get taxed
category_name: Extortion, cobro de piso and the trades that get taxed
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Extortion is sector-specific: the businesses with visible daily cash, fixed premises or predictable routes, which are disproportionately run and staffed by men.

title: Bad hombres
category_name: Being read as a criminal before you speak
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: A national political vocabulary that names Mexican men specifically as criminal, and the ordinary consequences of being the referent of a phrase everybody has heard.

title: Priced into the dating market
category_name: Being read as a criminal before you speak
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: The brief asked about men who are not dated because of what they are. There is measured platform data on this, and it is one of the better-evidenced rows in the psychological section.

title: Being suspected at every counter
category_name: Being read as a criminal before you speak
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The cumulative administrative cost of being treated as a probable problem by banks, landlords, employers and officials.

title: The deported man, at home
category_name: Being read as a criminal before you speak
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Return is not relief. Deportees are marked in Mexico - by accent, by tattoos, by the fact of having been sent back - and the stigma has a word.

title: The pigmentocracy at home
category_name: Discrimination inside Mexico: skin, class and language
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Skin tone predicts schooling and earnings inside Mexico, measurably and substantially. Discrimination against Mexican men does not begin at the border.

title: Indigenous, and that being a sentence
category_name: Discrimination inside Mexico: skin, class and language
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Indigenous Mexican men face compounded exclusion - language, documentation, land, and the internal agricultural migration circuit.

title: The Chinese in Mexico: a massacre and an expulsion
category_name: Discrimination inside Mexico: skin, class and language
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: The brief asked for weird, rare and non-obvious material. Mexico's own history of racial violence and mass expulsion is little known and well documented, and it complicates any simple account of who is excluded by whom.

title: Two surnames and a system with one box
category_name: Names, surnames, screening and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Mexican naming convention meets foreign database design, and the result is a man who does not match himself across records.

title: Sharing a name with somebody
category_name: Names, surnames, screening and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Common surnames plus watchlist matching produces men who are repeatedly stopped for someone else's record.

title: The officer who decided, and the one who would not have
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Identical facts producing opposite outcomes depending on who is at the window - the defining experience of discretionary systems.

title: The clerical error that becomes your record
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A wrong keystroke in an official system, and the years spent proving the system is wrong about you.

title: Four times more likely to kill himself
category_name: Being male: help-seeking, machismo, and dying of it
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Male suicide in Mexico runs at roughly four times the female rate, against a rising national trend - and the norms that produce it are the same ones that prevent him mentioning it.

title: Machismo, measured
category_name: Being male: help-seeking, machismo, and dying of it
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: The cultural expectation is not a cliché - it has been operationalised, measured, and associated with depression and reduced help-seeking, with effect sizes.

title: Not being read as a victim
category_name: Being male: help-seeking, machismo, and dying of it
applies_to_note: Triggered by being male
summary: The structural counterpart of VIO-001: men are the overwhelming majority of the killed and disappeared, and the least likely to be treated as victims by institutions, media or asylum systems.

title: The provider who cannot provide
category_name: Being male: help-seeking, machismo, and dying of it
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Where a man's standing rests on supporting a household, unemployment, injury or deportation is not a financial event but an identity one.

title: Informality means no health coverage
category_name: The health system, and the illnesses that arrive early
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Because more than half of Mexican work is informal, more than half of Mexican workers are outside the contributory health system - and the replacement schemes keep being restructured.

title: Illnesses that arrive twenty years early
category_name: The health system, and the illnesses that arrive early
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
summary: Diabetes, kidney disease and cardiovascular illness at ages that would be unusual elsewhere, in a population doing heavy physical work.

title: Treatment he will not seek
category_name: The health system, and the illnesses that arrive early
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Male under-use of preventive and primary care, compounded by language, cost and immigration fear where he is abroad.

title: The arithmetic that never stops
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Continuous background computation - status, money, risk, who is behind him, what the officer will ask - running underneath every ordinary task.

title: Not being able to plan
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Where status, safety and income are all revocable at short notice, long-horizon planning stops being rational - which is then read as fecklessness.

title: Being the threat in the room
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: The daily management of other people's fear of him, and what continuous self-monitoring costs.

title: Enforcement fear as an ambient condition
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: The fear of a raid or a stop operates on whole communities including citizens, and changes behaviour far beyond the people actually removable.

title: What it takes out of the work
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: The brief asked specifically about efficiency and growth. This is the row that says what the load does to output and to a career.

title: Divided across a line
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Living in one country with the people he loves in another, permanently, and what that does over decades.

title: Stress in the body, and the male-specific finding
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: The physiological cost of chronic stress is measurable as allostatic load - and in the largest Latino health study, the association held for men and not for women.

title: Depression arriving as a physical complaint
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Where distress cannot be named, it presents to a doctor as pain, fatigue or stomach trouble - and is treated as those things.

title: Sleep
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
summary: Short sleep as the common pathway through which long hours, second jobs, pain and vigilance convert into everything else.
